column49: Cohort_Experience_Text
I really appreciated the moral support of the group.
Rated fairly high because this model allowed me to make some very close friends but also was very stressful as far as academic schedule.
It worked well during the semester, but in spring when we "un-cohorted" it was difficult only knowing 20 other of the 150 students.  Usually only knew 2-3 people per class.

We really bonded.  As foundation progressed, we felt more comfortable sharing & discussing topics amongst each other.  Even into our second year, I still feel excited to see people from my cohort in my foundation semester.  There is a special bond there.  When people from my cohort are in my classes now, I feel more at ease in those classes.
The group of students I came in with were incredibe!  The only reason I didn't give a 10 rating is b/c the course content/structure of foundation was not ideal.

I liked the community feel that I got from my cohort; but once classes started mixing cohorts I felt like I didn't know any of them.  It would have been nice to have more opportunities to meet all of our entering class.

I liked the cohort system a lot.  It made me feel more comfortable being with the same people the whole year.  It was also nice finding friends (from your cohort) in classes in other semesters.  It was easier to express my opinion in class and present better.

Well this was my first initial experience just like others in foundation and I really didn't know what to expect.  I felt like the experience was enriching learning about how it works as well as gaining knowledge of the coursework.  I was pleased with my experience.
We had/have great chemistry and continue relying on each other for support.  We even continue sitting together in class.

My classmates becamse a support unit I was not expecting.  I laugh and talk about certain personal matters with people I would have thought no more than peers.  I encourage the continued use of the system.  Most people find their niche somewhere.  This gives them the space to do so.
Enjoyed the friendships made and kept 3 semesters later.
It was a great way to ease the beginning of the school connecting to other students.  The friends I made during the foundation semester are still escorting me to the last semester.
It is useful as it helps to develop friendships and collaborations easier and faster.  These relationships have then continued to be a part of my experience as a GCSW student.
I thought it was very effective in building relationships among colleagues.
It gave me a feeling of family - of belonging.  It helped me make friends faster.

I enjoyed meeting and fellowshipping with every one in my cohort (1), however the academic experience was a little disorganized.  It seemed as though we were the "test subjects" for new things that were implemented and there was little cohesiveness throughout my Foundation year.
Felt like I was a part of a community then when meeting others from different cohorts we had something to talk about (which cohort we were from).
I liked getting to know people better because we were all in the same classes.

I loved having the chance to get to know a group of people well.  We learned from one another on a personal and academic level.  While the classes did not always meet my expectations, my cohort made me look forward to attending class every week.

Foundation was eye opening in a very unique way.  I learned a lot I made some very strong friendships.  However, I was disapponted with some of the professors, classes, and assignments.  This is a graduate level program and the foundation semester did not reflect that.
The experience was what I expected coming from a simular undergraduate SW program.
I liked the cohort system because you were able to build friendships & relationships with potential collegues.

The cohort system was good and I loved it.  I was able to meet ppl that were from different diverse backgrounds.  The only thing is, is tthat it was hard splitting up from the foundation semester when it came to meeting other cohorts.  But overtime I got used to the other cohorts.  I have or i think i have attachment issues, so i believe i was slightly jealous seeing my cohort partners hanging w/other cohorts, but eventually it allowed me to branch off and expand relationships.

The cohort system is helpful in that it gives us a base of peers when starting grad school.  However, advanced standing are left out of the cohort/foundation system - big flaw in the program.  Also it seems cohorts were not put together with much intention - it was just based on when we could come to our mtg.  More intention would ensure a better fit for students.

The cohort system was helpful in meeting people and feeling comfortable in a new setting, however, I felt that it was really exclusive and hard to meet other people once we weren't in our cohorts anymore.
Although it was a good review of material from undergrad, a pervious BSW should have had more weight.
I really liked the cohort experience because it was nice to establish a network to work with throughout graduate school.
I liked having the chance to get to know the students in my cohort.  However, it would be tough for students who struggled to get to know/become friends with their fellow cohort members.
Neutral - neither the best or worst.
My cohort bonded very well & was incredibly supportive.  We helped to empower each other & it was wonderful being able to have shared experiences.
The cohort system provided a strong group of friends & colleagues.  The consistency of classmates mad e for quicker relationship forming and was by far the most enjoyable part of foundation.
It was like having a great family for support at a very new exciting but difficult time in my life.  My cohort is family to me.  They have helped me through my entire grad experience.
I really liked my cohort in general.  It was a good combination of people.  What I didn't like was the way foundation was handled.
Although I believe having cohorts is beneficial in some ways, I also believe that in a lot of ways it kept me from getting to know others outside of my designated cohort.
I liked it & would have liked to keep the cohort together through graduation.
I think the cohort system allowed for me as an incoming student, who was also new to Houston, to develop ties whereas we may not have.  It allowed for us to not feel like we were alone.
Did not particularly care for cohort members; found them to be difficult.
It was easy to get to know people and create longer lasting friendships.
Established foundation of network, but limited exposure to others.
As a cohort we are way to sensitive!  We never came to any conclusions & rarely debated any points of view.  I am glad the cohort experience is only one semester.
The cohort system served me well during foundation semester.  I still greatly respect cohort members but it has been difficult to maintain friendships due to time constraints.
Easier to make friends in a small cohort
The classmates are awesome!  They do care each other.
I feel most comfortable with my cohort.  However it made me feel less comfortable and on edge when around other cohorts.

My cohort seemed to mesh well.  There were a couple of people that caused some issues,  but overall we got along.  I became close friends with a handful of people from our cohort and have continued taking classes with them.  I didn't like that it was hard to meet people outside of our cohort.

In the beginning, the cohort unity  was a big help, much like running with a big group in a marathon, providing support and momentum.  A fellow cohort member created a facebook page for us which really got conversations going.  Any of us could find instant help with an assignment.  As time went on, I felt a backlash from my cohort for making outside relatinships.  They would self-segregate in classes, which I did not follow.  I now feel my cohort is rather close, and I am on the outside.
Feel the cohort system is great in making and building relationships.  Also tends to become somewhat exclusive if you don't reach out beyond your cohort.

I enjoyed being part of a small group and getting to know individuals.  However, there was no real opportunity to meet students from other cohorts.  Walking into class in the spring,  Ihad a class where I didn't know anyone.
I relly enjoyed having class with all of the same people.  There was one person who talked too much so it was greating a break from that in the 2nd semester.  I developed beneficial relationships.

Good structure, gave solid support system, bonding time.  Did not appreciate how secluded we were from the other cohorts.  Sometimes we were "stuck" in our ways/thinking and an outside perspective would have helped further learning.
Provided a sense of community and allowed for a support group.  Friendshiops have been a product of this system and it has been beneficial academically as well.
It was very effective and building relationships helped in many ways.  Owever I am an introvert so sometimes I revert back to keeping to myself.

I didn't see the benefits of being in a cohort.  I found it created clique mentalities.  Being in classes in which a mojority of the people came from a cohort other than my own really hindered the special/interactive process.  You get really close to 20 people for  months then you either part ways or clique up.
Being able to have colleagues that support one another.  Mycohort created strong bonds, relationships.  We all tend to flock to one another in classes outside of foundation.
I have made long lasting friendshipos that I feel have helped me evolve in the GCSW.
I met amazing people in my cohort.  Being in every class with them allowed us to form close bonds very quickly.

I think that a major reason I assimilated so rapidly and well into the GCSW was due to the cohort system.  I was able to form relationships with my fellow cohort students, and bond through our shared experience.  Having these friedships develop through regular shared class time also provided me support and resources for handling the course work.
It allowed me to have bonding ties with students.  Although we don't have the same classes this semester, we are always excited to see one another.
I was indifferent towards my cohort.  There wasn't a true community fostered in our group.

I like the idea of cohorts and know/interact more w/ppl from my cohort than others.  However I'm not very close to my cohort or all those in my cohort.  We're more friendly acquaintances, save a couple whom I'm closer to.

The cohort system allowed me to meet more of my peers than I might have on my own.  The cohort system created a little community for the cohort members.  They have been a great resource and support system for me, throughout my time at the GCSW.

I feel neutral about my cohort.  I have not become close with anyone except one person.  However, it was funny to see how everybody separated by race.  People became close Whites with Whites, Blacks with lacks, Hispanics with Hispanics and some poepel who were less outgoing was kind of left out.

One one hand.  I like the cohort system since it created a certain amount of time for me to get to know a particular group of folks.  I needed to interact with each of them in such structure.  Otherwise I would not have the opportunity to get familiar with them.  On the other hand it might decrease the chance for me to get to know other fellows in the GCSW.

I rated my experience to be in scale 8 because since I have been in this program I have learn a lot and I have also grown out of my shell.  I am more confident with my skin and I have wonderful professors.  By the end of my program I would have broaden my knowledge and also my skills.
I rarely socialize outside of school unless it's for an assignment so it was a basic experience for me.

I give my experience an 8 because I feel that I have gained professional and personal friendships in my cohort.  I enjoyed the bodn we all felt as a cohort.  The cohort system mad my first year of graduate school easier because I was not alone.
As much as I enjoyed having certain people as a constant support, the lack of extra diversity felt limiting.

The cohort system, as I experienced it, has created a cohesive, friendly base of people I can communicate with about school, work, & life (births, successes).  It is not a ten because I often feel there is reticence to communicate outside the cohort.
The cohort system is fine and I do feel like it was helpful, especially during the foundation.

Some members of my cohort do not work well together.  Even though we have gone through several classes together, we still have trouble working together.  I'm sure I was placed in this cohort because of my work hours and degree plan, but academicaly we are not all on the same leve, and because of the cohort I was placed in the degree plan delayed my time to graduate.

It was really great to have a built in group starting from day 1.  We have all gotten pretty close and it has enhanced my learning.  I gave it a 9 rather than a 10 because group texting can get out of control.

I was able to increase my network.  I had people who had similar experience and were able to be a support system during my first year at GCSW.  It made being in graduate school not as foreign as I expected it to be.
It was convenient to have a cohort during foundation because it allows us to have contact with the people who have all the same classes as you.

I rated my cohort experience a 10 because it helped to establish friendships and make the graduate school experience more comfortable.  I feel like my cohort is a team - there to encourrage and support one another through graduate school.  This feeling has been invaluable.
I loved coming in and knowing we were all learning at the same time how grad school worked.
I like the smaller classes with cohort 4 but I like meeting new people.  That being said I prefer meeting new people in each class.
Weekend cohort has turned into a weekend family.  It's great to go through this program w/people who supports and motivates you constantly.
Great to get to meet so many new MSW students, but being paired initially with another cohort was a little chaotic.
Working with this cohort has created a great relationship.  With working 40 hours a week, having a strong cohort to stick together and send reminders has been extremely helpful.
My cohort is great, we work well together.  This cohort complet a lot of teamwork.
I had the ability to build rapport with my classmates.  I was able to build a good support group that was helful during our difficult times of stress.

Because I have developed relationships with most everyone in the class.  Our group is a good support and network system. I'm not really friends per se with anyone outside of class, but I feel comfortable with my classmates enough ot contact them if I wanted to.
I enjoy being in a cohort because it allows me to create friendships and study partners.
Still centered around the other cohorts schedule.  Wish we could have entered into the foundation course, but I do understand why we couldn't.
I enjoy the networking opportunities and nw friends.  I enjoyed the professors.
My cohort has helped me stay in grad school & keep working towards graduation when I wanted to drop out.
Developed a focused & close study group that kept me motivated on completing assignmetns on or before the deadlines.
For the most part, the cohort system worked well for me in the foundation semester.
Development of relationshiops within cohort III due to sharing classes was broken after foundation.  Cohort 4 (WEC) is small & you know all, but cohort is divided into subgroups.

It's been easier keeping up with working full time & school by keeping same group together.  Everyone helps each other out once in a while they get on my nerves as I've learned more about my classmates, but it's more of a family type of get on your nerves.

I have had the opportunity to develop relationships within my cohort.  There have been several situations where we have collaborated together academically and worked during internships.  We are able to discuss issues and concerns that have had both positive/negative effect during the semester.  Visual individual I need pictures.

They help to keep me on track when I have a lot going on.  It helps because they give me reminders when assignemtns are due and I always have someone to study with if I want to.  It's comforting coming back to see familiar faces each semester.

I like the support that the cohort system builds.  Having peers that I know and have become friends with has helped me along this program.  I don't always love that we are locked in to certain things.  Overall, cohort system is great.

I chose the GCSW in part b/c it offered a cohort system.  I wanted to have a build in community w/in the college. So far it has been nice.  I don't feel that I've gotten to know people as much as I expected to, but I am still glad that I see the same faces in most of my classes.
In the advanced standing cohort
I'm advanced standing and we do not have a cohort
Advanced standing students have no cohort, therefore lacking the support system/network system that other students were alloted to.
I am advanced standing, therefore, not part of the cohort system
advanced standing
advanced standing student

I entered the GCSW as Advanced Standing and was not technically assigned a cohort.  However, as AS students, I feel as if we were given confusing or false infromation regarding classes, due dates, grad, etc.  A lot of miscommunication between students and staff.
I'm not in a cohort.
Advanced standing students are excluded from a lot of things.  We are kind of just "thrown in."
I am advanced standing.
Advanced standing students don't have a cohort.  Everything is set up for foundations students which is very frustrating.

I'm an advanced standing student and this cohort system is not really discussed.  It would be great to have some get togethers or something to get to know people in my "cohort" otherwise I don't really see a purpose for advanced standing.
N/A. Advanced standing
Advanced standing - no cohort.
I did not realy think that it made much of a difference.  Iwas in the Advance Standing group so this may be why.
